title: Lord, Lead the Way the Saviour Went
description: Lord, Lead the Way the Saviour Went in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER OLD, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: William Croswell wrote these words. They were printed in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 575, “He Went About Doing Good”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER OLD; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord, lead the way the Sa-viour went, By lane and cell ob-scure, And let our trea-sures still be spent, Like his, up-on the poor.

lines: Lord, lead the way the Saviour went,
And let our treasures still be spent,
Like him, through scenes of deep distress,
Who bore the world's sad weight,
For Thou hast placed us side by side
In this wide world of ill;
And that Thy followers may be tried,
The poor are with us still.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: William Croswell died in 1851.
credits: Words by William Croswell (1804–1851), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to WINCHESTER OLD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
